# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This landing page will contain an image
and a short text about the reasoning behind the book and what it is trying to achieve.


This books takes an developmental approach to visualization
motivating the introduction of each new principle or chart element
with the shortcoming of the previous.
This is because I have noticed that students of dat avisualization don't neceessarily 
**understand** when to use one type of chart instead of another.
Now they might still **remember** it becauase they have memorized some rule like
"never use bar chart for a mean" and then happily use a single point for the mean
that commit similar fouls without inspecting the underlying distribution of data.
**Understanding** instead of **remembering** is a way to empower students
to become their own agents and make predictions 
about what is good and what is bad outside the content of this book.
I hope to instill them with a critical thinking about any chart they might see
and not just remember that a certain chart time is good and another one is bad.
In my experience,that also makes things more fun.

To make the learning interactive, i also include code in many different libraries.
This focuses on grammars of graphics
because I think they do empower student in a similar way as descrbed above;
ie the predicatable grammar encourages students to understand 
what **could** work based on understasnding the structure and rules of the grammar
rather than being focused on what **does** work from remembering a full api catalogue 
of chart templtaes and names.

Just like development does not recapitulate the stags of evolution,
there progression herein is not a reflection of the history of data visualization
although this author think it could have been.
